title: CHAPTER 6: TRIBAL COMMUNITIES OF MADHYA PRADESH

blocks.content: 6.1 Overview of Tribes in Madhya Pradesh

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Madhya Pradesh has the largest tribal population in India in terms of absolute numbers.
The state is home to prominent major tribal groups including Bhil, Gond, Korku, and Kol.
Three tribal communities in MP are officially recognized as Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs): Baiga, Bharia, and Sahariya.
Rich cultural traditions are preserved through major tribal festivals such as Bhagoria, Madai, and Meghnath.

blocks.content: Madhya Pradesh has the highest Scheduled Tribe (ST) population in India in absolute numbers. Tribal communities constitute approximately 21% of the state's total population. The tribal belt is concentrated primarily in eastern, central-southern, and western parts of the state. The state has 46 Scheduled Tribes, of which several are Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs).

cells: Largest tribe in MP; Gond Paintings; Kachhi Ghodi dance

blocks.content: Madhya Pradesh has several Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) - formerly called Primitive Tribal Groups. These communities are considered especially vulnerable due to their declining or stagnant population, pre-agricultural technology, and critical economic situation.

items: Baiga - Mandla, Dindori, Umaria (shifting cultivation practitioners called Bewar)
Agaria - Mandla, Dindori (iron smelters, considered sacred craftsmen)

Bhagoria Haat (Bhil/Bhilala) - Marriage market festival of Jhabua, Alirajpur; celebrated in Phalgun month before Holi
Hareli (Gond) - First festival of year, sowing of seeds
Karma Festival - Worship of Karma tree for good harvest
Goncha Festival - Gond festival of Bastar region
Madai Festival - Tribal fair held in various parts of eastern MP
